content:
frank: Quick report — our async worker crashed when the API returned a 422 as text/plain. The py SDK called await resp.json() and raised JSONDecodeError which escaped the task. No structured SDK error to catch.
dina: that's annoying. The SDK should normalize non-2xx responses into a typed exception (e.g., RedwoodAPIError) and always attach raw_body when parsing fails. That way callers can inspect message/status without dealing with JSONDecodeError.
leo: agreed. proposed minimal shape: class RedwoodAPIError(Exception): status_code:int; message:str; raw_body:Optional[str]; request_id:Optional[str]; def is_retryable(self)->bool: return status_code>=500
pat: small but important: retry middleware currently retries on any exception from http layer. If JSONDecodeError bubbles out for a 4xx, it triggers retries and duplicates. Retry logic should consult err.is_retryable when available, otherwise fall back to network/5xx heuristics.
dina: implementation note: in http._handle_response try: parsed = await resp.json() except Exception as parse_exc: parsed = None; raw = await resp.text(); if resp.status < 300: return parsed if parsed is not None else raw; else: msg = parsed.get('detail') if isinstance(parsed, dict) and 'detail' in parsed else raw; err = RedwoodAPIError(resp.status, msg, raw_body=raw, request_id=resp.headers.get('x-request-id')); err.__cause__ = parse_exc; raise err
leo: add unit tests: text/plain 422 -> RedwoodAPIError with raw_body set and is_retryable False; json 422 -> parsed detail; 503 -> is_retryable True and gets retried; ensure sync client parity (requests raises ValueError).
pat: also add a tiny docs snippet for quickstart showing how to catch RedwoodAPIError in background tasks.
ci-bot: Created issue #2579: "py SDK: normalize error shape for non-json responses and tighten retry defaults"
frank: thanks — this will stop our workers from dying on unexpected content types and avoid duplicate writes. :thumbsup:
